sector: Healthcare - Medical Devices (Ophthalmic Surgical / ICL refractive)
drawdown_context: STAA traded near $30 going into 2025 and was at $18.29 on 2025-05-15 (~-62% drawdown from 52-wk highs). FY24 swung to a $20.2M net loss vs $21.3M net income in FY23 after 10 consecutive years of growth, driven by a Q4 2024 collapse in China ICL distributor reorders. The pre-cutoff Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-07) confirmed China revenue fell from $38.5M to $0.4M YoY (-99%), the company took a $22.7M restructuring/impairment charge, CEO Tom Frinzi was replaced by Stephen C. Farrell (Feb 26, 2025), and CFO Patrick Williams was replaced by Deborah Andrews as Interim CFO. Forward return +77.5% in the 12 months after cutoff confirms a survivor.

rfm_tuples.R: For the fiscal year ended December 27, 2024, we reported $313.9 million of net sales, a decrease of 3% compared to $322.4 million in fiscal 2023, and we incurred a net loss of $20.2 million compared to net income of $21.3 million in fiscal 2023. Prior to fiscal 2024, we had reported over ten years of annual net sales growth, and we had delivered net income profitability since 2018. Our results in fiscal 2024 were negatively impacted by a significant decline in ICL sales in China in the fourth quarter ended December 27, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: Does the 10-K present the FY24 reversal in plain quantitative terms, name the cause (China), and avoid euphemism? Mode A internal filing audit.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Disclosure is direct: dollar revenue and net loss are stated up front; the 10-year growth-streak break is explicitly acknowledged; China is named as the proximate cause. No 'temporary headwind' / 'one-time' language used; risk factors lead with 'We reported a decrease in revenue and a net loss in fiscal 2024, and we may not be able to return to our growth and profitability trajectory.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest framing of the worst FY in a decade. The fact that the risk factor leads with 'we may not be able to return to growth' is unusually candid for a med-device issuer.

rfm_tuples.R: Two customers, our China distributors who sell into China and Hong Kong, accounted for approximately 51% of our consolidated net sales during fiscal 2024. Net sales to our China distributors during each of the last three fiscal years: 2024 $161,321 (51.4%); 2023 $185,554 (57.6%); 2022 $148,167 (52.1%).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: Customer concentration disclosure check. Are exact distributor names and shares given over multi-year history with no obfuscation?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Two named China distributors disclosed as ~51% of consolidated sales, with 3-year history showing the concentration has been structural (52% / 58% / 51%), not new. Risk factor explicitly says 'if our China distributors, which accounted for approximately 51% of our fiscal 2024 consolidated net sales, ceased to serve as our distributors, or significantly underperformed our expectations, we may experience [adverse impact].'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Concentration disclosure is complete and multi-year. They name the structural single-country dependency that drove the drawdown. Not hiding the ball.

rfm_tuples.R: Inventory Days on Hand (DOH) was 194 and 142 days for 2024 and 2023, respectively, for finished goods, including consignment inventory. In fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024, we increased our production and inventory to support anticipated sales growth of ICL products... our distributors in China held, as of December 27, 2024, elevated levels of ICL product inventory.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: Channel stuffing/inventory build tell. Med-device with distributor model and DOH expansion + customer down-purchasing is the classic 'demand was always weaker than reported' pattern. Verify the disclosure addresses both the company-side inventory bloat AND distributor-side inventory bloat.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Both sides of the inventory bloat are disclosed: company DOH 194 days (vs 142 LY = +37% build) AND explicit acknowledgment that China distributors are sitting on elevated finished-goods stock from above-minimum bulk purchases ahead of an expected high season that did not materialize. The Q1 2025 10-Q confirms the unwinding: China sales went $38.5M to $0.4M as distributors satisfied procedural demand from existing inventory.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A is PASS - they did disclose the inventory bloat. Mode B is a moderate concern: the 'channel inventory was built in anticipation of high season that did not materialize' framing is the kind of explanation that historically precedes 1-2 more quarters of sell-through pain. The 10-Q proves the company's own H1 2025 'minimal China revenue' warning was accurate, which actually de-risks subsequent quarters.

rfm_tuples.R: [$3.9 million of cost of sales associated with our shipment of $27.5 million of ICLs to one of our distributors in China in the quarter] As the control of the inventory transferred to the distributor, accounting rules require us to record the costs of sales upon such transfer, even if revenue is not recognized... While we did not recognize revenue on this order upon shipment, we believe that having these ICLs in-country in China can help address challenges and delays associated with shipping products to China.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: Revenue-recognition aggressiveness check. Look for shipments deferred for collectibility reasons - that's a soft going-concern signal on the distributor side. Does the company explain WHY revenue wasn't recognized?
rfm_tuples.M_value: $27.5M shipment had cost-of-sales recognized but revenue deferred. The 'explanation' is logistics ('having ICLs in-country can help address shipping delays'), but the more obvious read is collectibility/sell-through doubt at the distributor. The company is not hiding the fact (it's flagged explicitly as a gross-margin item), but the reason given understates the distress signal. The Q1 2025 10-Q later reframes this as tariff-mitigation consignment (post-cutoff context: tariff announced Feb 1, 2025).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest about the mechanics but soft on the implication. Shipping $27.5M with no revenue recognition because the distributor's ability to sell-through is uncertain is a textbook distressed-channel tell. Mode A PASS (disclosed); Mode B moderate concern.

rfm_tuples.R: We had $144.2 million of cash and cash equivalents and $86.3 million of investments available for sale at December 27, 2024. Our current liquidity and capital resources, as discussed above, will enable us to meet our known contractual obligations as of December 27, 2024. [No long-term debt or credit facility borrowings disclosed.]
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: Liquidity adequacy check. Is the 'sufficient liquidity' claim backed by actual balance-sheet evidence and absence of debt covenants?
rfm_tuples.M_source: filing_text_audit (internal); Liquidity and Capital Resources section
rfm_tuples.M_value: $230M of cash + investments, $297.6M working capital, no long-term debt, no credit facility borrowings, no covenant risk. Even with FY24 operating loss and Q1 2025 $57M operating loss (per 10-Q), runway is multi-year. No going-concern language, no substantial-doubt qualifier.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Cash-rich, debt-free balance sheet is the dominant survival-signal here. Even an apocalyptic China year does not threaten solvency. This is the single biggest factor separating STAA from a fraud/short candidate.

rfm_tuples.R: The report of BDO USA, P.C., our independent registered public accounting firm... /s/ BDO USA, P.C. Los Angeles, California February 21, 2025. We have served as the Company's auditor since 1993. [ICFR] effective as of December 27, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: auditor_change_tracker - check auditor continuity, tier, disagreements, ICFR opinion, restatement triggers.
rfm_tuples.M_value: BDO USA (tier-2, not Big 4) has audited since 1993 - 32-year continuity. Unqualified opinion. ICFR effective. No material weakness. No restatement / Rule 10D-1 clawback trigger. Critical Audit Matter is deferred-tax valuation allowance - reasonable for an issuer with a fresh net loss.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Tier-2 auditor is a slight historical concern for a $300M+ revenue issuer but the 32-year continuity and clean opinion offset. No auditor change adjacent to the bad-news disclosure - that would have been the red-flag pattern. PASS.

rfm_tuples.R: [Pre-cutoff 10-Q filed 2025-05-07] In the first quarter of 2025, the Company took a number of steps to change its leadership team, realign its leadership structure to better address market needs, reduce certain non-strategic activities and reposition the Company to return to sustainable growth... severance, reduction in workforce, and consulting expenses of $9,447,000; impairment expenses on leasehold improvements and machinery and equipment of $7,059,000... internally developed software [impairment] $2,751,000... aggregate $22,664,000. [Exhibits:] Employment Agreement, effective February 26, 2025, by and between the Company and Stephen C. Farrell. Consulting Agreement, effective February 26, 2025, by and between the Company and Thomas G. Frinzi. /s/ DEBORAH ANDREWS, Interim Chief Financial Officer.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: Claim evolution between 10-K (Feb 21, 2025) and pre-cutoff 10-Q (May 7, 2025) - the strongest 'lying' tell. Also CEO/CFO transitions clustered to bad-news disclosure (insider_vs_calendar). 10-K signed by Frinzi as CEO on Feb 21; 5 days later (Feb 26) Frinzi transitions to consulting and Stephen Farrell becomes CEO. CFO Patrick Williams is gone - replaced by Interim CFO Andrews.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Both CEO and CFO turned over within 5 days of the 10-K signing. The 10-K's 'we believe Q1 2025 will normalize' tone was overwritten by the 10-Q's -45% YoY revenue ($77.4M -> $42.6M total, $38.5M -> $0.4M in China), $22.7M restructuring charge, and full leadership replacement. The 10-K did warn that China would be weak in H1 2025 ('we anticipate we will report minimal China ICL sales in the first half of fiscal 2025') so the magnitude is consistent with disclosed guidance - but the leadership shake-up was NOT pre-signalled.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A is mostly PASS - the bad news magnitude tracked the 10-K guidance. Mode B is a moderate concern: the CEO/CFO/COO turnover clustered to the worst quarter in a decade is a classic 'house cleaning' pattern, but in this case it's being done WITH the bad-news disclosure rather than AFTER it - which is honest. The new-CEO+restructuring+impairment combo is the typical kitchen-sink quarter that often marks the operational trough.

rfm_tuples.R: [Forward-looking statements / risk factors] On February 1, 2025, the U.S. government announced a 10% tariffs on product imports from certain countries, including China. In response, China announced that they would impose counter tariffs of 10% to 15% on select goods imported from the U.S. If maintained, the newly announced tariffs and the potential escalation of trade disputes between China and the U.S. would adversely impact our sales and operations in the region.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: Tariff/geopolitical exposure timing. 10-K was filed Feb 21, 2025 - 20 days after the Feb 1 tariff. Did management address tariff risk fresh-and-specifically, or hide behind boilerplate? Cross-reference with Q1 2025 10-Q for action taken.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K names the Feb 1 tariff by date and quantifies (10% US tariff on China imports, 10-15% Chinese counter-tariffs). The 10-Q discloses the actual mitigation action: 'In April 2025, in order to mitigate potential financial exposure from such tariffs, we negotiated and implemented consignment agreements with our two distributors in China, and we delivered consigned inventory to China in advance of the implementation of tariffs.' That's a concrete operational response, not a wait-and-see hedge.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Tariff disclosure is specific, dated, and followed by concrete action. The consignment restructuring is a real operational response, not a press-release-only move. This is honest-issuer behavior.

rfm_tuples.R: During the quarter ended December 27, 2024, no director or officer (as defined in Rule 16a-1(f) under the Exchange Act) of the Company adopted or terminated any Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangements or any non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement (in each case, as defined in Item 408(a) of Regulation S-K).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: insider_vs_calendar - check for 10b5-1 plan adoptions/terminations clustered to the Q4 2024 bad-news quarter. Also check the absence of opportunistic insider activity (no share repurchases announced during the drawdown either).
rfm_tuples.M_value: No 10b5-1 activity in Q4 2024. No buyback program disclosed/active during the drawdown ($230M cash but no buyback authorization deployment). The 10-K shows $7.4M from option exercises and $1.5M used to repurchase shares for tax-withholding only - not a real buyback. So neither the 'insiders selling into bad news on 10b5-1' pattern nor the 'company buying back at all-time lows' opportunism pattern is present. Pure inaction on capital allocation during the drawdown.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Absence of 10b5-1 sales is a (weak) positive honesty signal. But the absence of a buyback during a -60% drawdown with $230M cash and no debt is itself a soft 'management does not have conviction' signal. Without external form4 corroboration this is marked UNV; the negative-space read is non-committal.

rfm_tuples.R: [Pre-cutoff 10-Q] While the level of inventory owned by our distributors in China has decreased substantially since December 27, 2024, we believe their ICL inventory is likely sufficient to meet currently expected procedure volumes for at least the first half of fiscal 2025. We therefore anticipate we will report minimal China ICL sales in the first half of fiscal 2025. As China in-country inventory is reduced during the first half of fiscal 2025, we would expect our China revenue to normalize.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: Forward-guidance honesty. Issuer issued specific, falsifiable forward statement ('minimal China sales H1 2025'). Verify that this is a real (bad) guide rather than disguised optimism. Test against actual Q1 2025 result.
rfm_tuples.M_source: filing_text_audit (internal); 10-Q forward statement vs reported Q1 result
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 China revenue $0.4M (vs $38.5M YoY, -99%) directly confirms the 'minimal China sales' guidance was accurate, not aspirational. Total revenue -45% YoY. Operating loss $57.4M including restructuring. Management told the market the truth about H1 2025 weakness BEFORE the cutoff, with enough specificity to be falsifiable.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Falsifiable forward statement that matched bad reality. This is a strong honesty-alpha PASS. The company guided down hard before the cutoff and delivered the bad H1 they promised - which is exactly the setup where post-cutoff snapback occurs once the kitchen sink is fully visible.

supplemental_signals.going_concern_language: ABSENT - no going-concern or substantial-doubt language in either the 10-K or pre-cutoff 10-Q
supplemental_signals.auditor_continuity: BDO USA continues; tier-2 (not Big 4); 32-year tenure since 1993; unqualified opinion, ICFR effective
supplemental_signals.icfr: Effective as of 12/27/2024; no material weakness disclosed
supplemental_signals.covenant_status: N/A - no long-term debt, no credit facility borrowings; pure cash-and-investments balance sheet
supplemental_signals.share_repurchase: No active buyback program deployed during drawdown despite $230M cash and no debt; only tax-withholding repurchases ($1.5M)
supplemental_signals.claim_evolution_10K_vs_10Q: PRESENT and tracked. 10-K (Feb 21, 2025) said H1 2025 China would be minimal; 10-Q (May 7, 2025) confirmed Q1 China revenue $0.4M (-99% YoY). Plus 10-Q revealed (a) CEO change (Frinzi -> Farrell, Feb 26, 2025), (b) CFO change (Williams -> Andrews Interim), (c) $22.7M restructuring/impairment charge, (d) consignment restructuring with China distributors to mitigate tariffs. The kitchen-sink-and-leadership-reset is a textbook trough setup, not a deception pattern.
supplemental_signals.insider_form4: No 10b5-1 plan adoptions/terminations in Q4 2024 per Item 408
supplemental_signals.customer_concentration: 51% from 2 China distributors (2024), 58% (2023), 52% (2022) - structural and disclosed
supplemental_signals.tariff_exposure: Specifically dated (Feb 1, 2025 US 10% on China imports; China 10-15% retaliatory). Mitigation: April 2025 consignment agreements with both China distributors and consigned inventory delivered pre-tariff.
supplemental_signals.tone: 10-K tone is candid (leads risk factors with 'we may not be able to return to growth and profitability'). 10-Q tone is more contrite given the new-CEO/restructuring overlay. No promotional adjectives in bad-news disclosures.
supplemental_signals.honesty_alpha_view: STAA is structurally a clean honesty-alpha LONG-tier (or at minimum non-SHORT) name. Massive customer concentration risk + bad single-country shock + leadership turnover would superficially scream SHORT, but the company (a) disclosed the concentration multi-year, (b) gave falsifiable forward guidance that turned out accurate, (c) has $230M cash and no debt, (d) replaced leadership and took kitchen-sink charges WITH the bad news rather than hiding them, (e) executed real operational mitigation (consignment). Framework should EXCLUDE from short candidates; the +77.5% forward return is consistent with a 'fully disclosed trough + cash-rich + new leadership' setup.

summary: STAA's FY24 10-K and pre-cutoff Q1 2025 10-Q together represent a textbook honest-issuer response to a severe customer-concentration shock. The company candidly disclosed the structural ~51% China-distributor dependency (multi-year), the 194-day inventory DOH, the $27.5M deferred-revenue shipment, the Feb 1 tariff exposure, and gave a falsifiable forward guide ('minimal China sales H1 2025') that proved accurate when Q1 China revenue collapsed 99% to $0.4M. Management replaced both CEO (Frinzi -> Farrell, Feb 26) and CFO (Williams -> Andrews Interim) WITH the bad news, took a $22.7M restructuring/impairment charge, and executed real operational mitigation (consignment agreements pre-tariff). Critically, the balance sheet is $230M cash/investments with NO long-term debt - solvency is untouchable. BDO continuity since 1993, ICFR effective, no going-concern. 6 PASS / 3 MODERATE / 0 SEVERE / 0 RED / 1 UNV. The framework should mark this as a NON-SHORT (LONG-tier or NEUTRAL) - which is the correct call given the +77.5% forward return. This is the canonical 'cleared deck + leadership reset + cash-rich' trough setup, the opposite of a fraud pattern.
